source_snapshot.procedure: Open Settings > User Management, then change an existing user's password, username and privilege.
source_snapshot.criteria: After password change only the new password logs in; after username change only the new name logs in; after privilege change only functions allowed by the new privilege are usable.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes an operator-driven write but conflates account actions, uses insecure partial list readback and does not isolate password/username/privilege changes, protect old/new secrets, define username/session semantics, prove old/new login/effective authorization or restore state.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL risk correctly requires one disposable account, immutable ID, one property per approved action, complete state/audit after each, old/new credential and session behavior, non-destructive role enforcement, independent recovery and cleanup.

old_problem: Password, username and privilege are three different authentication/authorization mutations with different acceptance and recovery; executing them cumulatively can hide which change caused a failure. A final account list cannot prove old-secret denial, username alias removal, stable identity, effective role boundaries or session invalidation. Target policy and disposable values can be parameterized while retaining all three checkpoints.
disposition_reason: Run password, username and privilege as three independently approved subtests from the same known disposable-account baseline, restoring and proving baseline equality between them. Require actual WebUI visuals, complete account/session/audit readback and functional old/new login or allow/deny results. Username N/A is permitted only with authoritative target evidence that renaming is unsupported; it cannot be silently omitted. Values and session rules are Project inputs, not unresolved engineering logic.
decision_basis: XLSX row 938, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, adjacent Delete-User/IPMI-View rows and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed; row 939 and its manifest identity were independently verified.
The three source Criteria independently require password authentication, username authentication and privilege enforcement; final list state or one combined change cannot satisfy all three.
ED-20/ED-23 require actual WebUI visual operation/evidence, while ED-35 prohibits API-only substitution for the functional mutations.

DMTF ManagerAccount identity/role/enabled fields and SessionService can corroborate persistence and session behavior, but password values remain secret and effective authorization requires bounded functional checks.

test_case.test_name: Independently modify and restore disposable account password, username and privilege through WebUI
test_case.purpose: Verify in three independent restore cycles that the BMC WebUI changes a disposable account's password, username and privilege correctly: only the new secret authenticates, only the new username authenticates while stable account identity remains controlled, and the new role permits and denies exactly the approved functions; each cycle preserves protected access and returns to baseline before the next.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware/WebUI build and authoritative password, username mutability/case/duplicate, role, lockout/rate-limit and session-invalidation semantics
One disposable non-production account with stable member ID/slot, baseline username, baseline least-privilege role and protected baseline/new/restore secrets
Three independent subtest specifications: password old/new/restore; username old/new/restore; role old/new/restore with non-destructive allow/deny matrix
Authoritative applicability evidence if username rename is unsupported; UI absence alone is insufficient for N/A
Complete trusted account/role/session/audit baseline, protected/recovery-account list and independent local-admin/console recovery
Per-subtest point-of-action approval, visual capture/redaction, bounded login/session test and exact restore/delete cleanup plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL AUTHENTICATION/AUTHORIZATION WRITES; THREE SEPARATE APPROVALS REQUIRED. Preserve logs, verify target/recovery and capture the disposable account's stable ID/slot, username, role, state and sessions. For each subtest start from and later restore the same proven baseline; never carry a modified state into the next. (A) Password: human changes only the secret through WebUI, captures redacted visual/audit evidence, proves new secret login succeeds and old secret login is denied within rate-limit policy, checks session behavior, then restores/rotates. (B) Username: if authoritative target semantics support it, change only username, prove the same stable account has the new name, new-name login succeeds and old-name login is denied, then restore; otherwise record authoritative N/A. (C) Privilege: change only RoleId/privilege to the approved alternate least-risk role, prove the mapped allowed and denied non-destructive operations from a new session, then restore. After every cycle collect complete trusted UI/API/session state and prove baseline equality. Do not expose secrets, modify protected accounts, clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Password cycle changes no field except secret-related audit/state; new secret authenticates, old secret is denied and sessions follow policy. Username cycle preserves the intended stable account/slot while only the new username authenticates and the old name is absent/denied, or has authoritative unsupported N/A. Privilege cycle changes only the role and enforces every approved allow/deny boundary without broader access. Each cycle shows actual WebUI success, complete readback/audit, protected/local recovery continuity and exact baseline restoration before the next.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Each subtest has an independent verdict and restore gate. Password PASS requires new-success/old-denial; username PASS requires stable identity, new-success/old-denial (or authoritative N/A); privilege PASS requires exact persisted role and all allowed/denied checks. All require actual WebUI visuals, session-policy evidence, unrelated-field equality, recovery and restore. UI toast, account-list output or RoleId alone cannot pass. Old credential/name remaining valid unexpectedly, wrong identity/role, over/under privilege, secret exposure, lockout, protected-account/session impact or restore failure is FAIL and stops later subtests. Missing policy/values/recovery/approval is NOT READY.
safety_gate: Use only a disposable account; never modify a protected, production, sole-admin or recovery identity and never reuse production secrets.
Protect old/new/restore passwords and tokens from screenshots, DOM, browser history, commands, logs and records; store only redacted outcomes.
Run one property per cycle with separate approval and exact restore proof before the next; stop on any unexpected field/session/audit change.
Use bounded new-session login and non-destructive authorization tests that honor lockout/rate limits; do not brute-force or retry automatically.
Actual WebUI operation and visual evidence are mandatory; API readback only corroborates. Username N/A requires authoritative capability evidence.
expected_evidence: Target/account policy, three-subtest matrix, disposable stable ID/slot, protected-account exclusions, redacted baseline and recovery proof
Per-subtest human WebUI visual/audit evidence with exactly one changed property and complete trusted persisted-state readback
Password new-login success/old denial and session result without secret content
Username stable-identity/new-login/old denial or authoritative unsupported evidence; privilege allowed/denied functional matrix
Per-cycle exact restore and final baseline equality, preserved logs/no secret exposure and three independent engineer verdicts
test_case.recovery: On lockout, wrong rename/role, unexpected session/access behavior or restore failure, stop all later subtests without retry. Use independent local-admin/console recovery to restore the disposable account's exact baseline username/role/state and rotate/reset its secret under separate approval, close/revoke test sessions per policy, preserve audit evidence and verify protected accounts remain unchanged.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require three account-property modifications and matching functional behavior. Target values and username support/session policy are explicit parameterized readiness inputs.

blocked.reason: Password, username and privilege cycles, evidence and recovery are defined. A safe disposable target and policies can be supplied; unsupported username change can be authoritative N/A.
